items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: Maybe a John Robichaud's band, or Emmanuel Peres's band, or one of those bands.

ctx.x: Now, what about the different time signatures they used to use there? Would they play much six-eighths music and dances?

No, I mean, when they had the picnics, like at the fairground, I mean, well, that was a different story. You see the picnics at the fairground, when they had, like the bulls would give a picnic, a lion or the two-layer, the Aiden Social Pleasure Club. One of those would give a picnic, you know. At the fairground, well, they'd have three bands, you see. Downstairs, in the big hall, they'd have the, either the Excelsior Brass Band or the OBBs, the Ormond Brass Band, see. And they'd play, they'd play the marches.…
Well, what sort of deal did they have set up in the field? Would they have a bar out there or something? Well, yeah, they had all that, no, they had all that, yeah, they had a little bar out there.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band.

ctx.x: If you could run through that, do you remember? Yeah, I heard them.

Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band. And he had Buddy Johnson on trombone at that time. And he had Baby Matthews on drums. And he had George Buckhead on clarinet. And Willie Santiago on the guitar. And Jimmy Brown played the bass. That was Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Superior Band. Now, pardon me. The Superior Band, in that band, I, when I first seen that band, they had, uh, uh, uh, Mac Murray on drums. They had, uh, Cock and Rumble…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: Manuel Perez, Joe Oliver, and Kimball.

ctx.x: They don't have no musicians. No, shame on them.

You should hear those bands in those days, like the Olympia band, Superior band, and Imperial band, those was bands. And the parade, does he like the Armand Brass band? I mean, well, the Armand Brass band, I mean, they played my father, I mean, he can't tell you about that, because you didn't ask him about that. But I can tell you, they played ball house music. You can forget about what he said about the other fellas, you know, reading at that time. Yeah, but later on in the years, I mean, it was a Ball House…
Who were the Ball House men in that band?
